newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia advisor says sell off only part of oil firm.
newsitem.headline: Serbia advisor says sell off only part of oil firm.

text.p: Serbia should privatise only parts of its oil company NIS Jugopetrol and invest the proceeds upgrading the rest of the company, a Serbian government expert said on Thursday.

"It would not be very wise for the entire NIS Jugopetrol to be transformed, but only some parts of it," said Dragan Djuricin, a member of the government advisory team helping prepare the privatisation.
"Privatisation receipts should be then used to increase the capital and for restructuring of the rest of the company."
He said the bill for the first time envisages state property to be a subject of transformation and privatisation which was a very positive sign.
"NIS Jugopetrol is a utility enterprise and as such belongs to the state. The bill on ownership transformation envisages that founders of NIS take decision on its transformation," said Djuricin.

Serbia under a privatisation law due for adoption in June is preparing privatisation programmes for the country's big, strategically important companies, infrastructure systems and indebted firms. Serbia's oil company will also be transformed under one of such plans, Djuricin said.
"The transformation programme should define the percentage of the enterprise for transformation, part of the system to be transformed and the model of privatisation as envisaged by the law."
The draft envisages sell-offs, capital increase, debt-for-equity-swaps and a combination of privatisation models for state-owned companies.
Djuricin explained that when transforming NIS Jugopetrol, existing law on transformation of utility firms must also be respected.
"According to the law, state must keep a majority or at least 51 percent of the stake in the transformed enterprise."
He said the oil company was attractive because of its profit potential, but to transform it needed changes to the monopoly law and regulations on imports, quotas, prices."
